findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the retention premise with the actual code: either introduce DOCKER_IMAGE_RETAIN as NEW work (it does not exist) or restate §2/its AC to match autodeploy.sh's existing orphan sweep (mcp_reconcile_orphans keeps only live + prev, sweeps containerless per-release tags — no keep-N-oldest count).
evidence: Plan: 'held by the repo's existing rollback-safe retention: docker image prune -f (dangling) each cycle, plus … a bounded sweep of the oldest per-release compose-mcp:<sha> tags beyond DOCKER_IMAGE_RETAIN (default 3) via docker image rm WITHOUT -f'

autodeploy.sh:577-602 mcp_reconcile_orphans keeps exactly live_ref + prev_ref (MCP_PREV_SHA_FILE) and removes ALL OTHER orphaned per-release <40-hex> tags — it sweeps containerless orphans, not 'surplus beyond a retain count of 3'; there is no 'keep the N oldest' semantic
autodeploy.sh:521 'narrowed to exactly the images whose container has been reaped' — orphan-driven, not count-driven
findings.finding: The plan attributes a count-based retention ('a bounded sweep of the oldest per-release compose-mcp:<sha> tags beyond DOCKER_IMAGE_RETAIN (default 3)') to the repo's EXISTING retention, but no DOCKER_IMAGE_RETAIN exists in the repo and the existing sweep is not count-based.
findings.location: Design §2 'Image/layer share (15 GiB) — RETENTION'; AC 'Over-share retention sweeps only surplus per-release tags via docker image rm without -f'
scenarios: Implementer wires the image/layer share to a non-existent DOCKER_IMAGE_RETAIN=3 knob and a retain-N-oldest sweep that the existing autodeploy.sh does not implement, silently diverging from the actual mcp_reconcile_orphans (live+prev only) behavior.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the image/layer-share description: either introduce a real `DOCKER_IMAGE_RETAIN` (default 3) knob in docker-storage-cap.sh/autodeploy.sh, or restate the sweep as the actual live+prev-only preservation implemented by mcp_reconcile_orphans (no count-based retain).
evidence: Plan: 'a bounded sweep of the oldest per-release compose-mcp:<sha> tags beyond DOCKER_IMAGE_RETAIN (default 3) via docker image rm WITHOUT -f'
autodeploy.sh:592 preserves only live_ref and prev_ref (recorded previous release) — no N=3 retention count
findings.finding: The plan's Design §2 (Image/layer share) names a `DOCKER_IMAGE_RETAIN` knob (default 3) that bounds the over-share sweep of 'the oldest per-release compose-mcp:<sha> tags beyond DOCKER_IMAGE_RETAIN', but no `DOCKER_IMAGE_RETAIN` symbol exists in the repo and the referenced consumer (autodeploy.sh mcp_reconcile_orphans, near :554) implements a live+prev-only sweep with no count-based retention of 3.
scenarios: An implementer looking for DOCKER_IMAGE_RETAIN finds no such knob; the described count-of-3 semantics contradict the actual live+prev-only preservation the AC then affirms.
findings.suggested_fix: Restate as: the sweep removes surplus per-release <sha> tags via `docker image rm` (no -f), preserving the live backend image and the recorded previous release ($MCP_PREV_SHA_FILE); drop the non-existent DOCKER_IMAGE_RETAIN/default-3 reference.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the third alarm's name: the plan says `rebar-docker-unaccounted-overlay2` but the artifact/runbook use `rebar-docker-unaccounted-bytes` — pick one and make plan, terraform, and runbook agree.
findings.finding: The plan names the orphaned-overlay2 alarm `rebar-docker-unaccounted-overlay2`, but the artifact it must declare/pin is named `rebar-docker-unaccounted-bytes` (terraform resource alarm_name and runbook table). The AC pins alarms 'by name', so the named target and the real artifact disagree.
findings.location: Plan §Alarms item 3 and AC 'Terraform declares the three alarms... pinned by name'
scenarios: test_alarm_actions_terraform.py pins alarms by name; a name-mismatch between plan and artifact makes the AC's 'pinned by name' ambiguous about which name is authoritative.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the plan reference to `rebar-docker-unaccounted-bytes` to match the declared terraform resource and runbook.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the compose-up.sh anchor: `systemctl enable --now docker` is at line 88 (not 55) and `dnf install -y docker` (line 53) precedes it, so it is not the first side-effecting step; the cap must merge ahead of the systemctl call specifically.
evidence: Plan: 'The merge goes into compose-up.sh ahead of systemctl enable --now docker (today's first side-effecting step, line 55)'
compose-up.sh:88 'systemctl enable --now docker' — the command is at line 88, not 55
compose-up.sh:53 'dnf install -y docker' is a side-effecting step that runs before it, so it is not the 'first side-effecting step'
findings.finding: The plan pins compose-up.sh's install point to '`systemctl enable --now docker` … (today's first side-effecting step, line 55)', but that command is at line 88 and an earlier side-effecting step (`dnf install -y docker`, line 53) precedes it.
findings.location: Design 'Install point, and how a LIVE daemon picks it up'
scenarios: An implementer or reviewer navigates to line 55 expecting the systemctl call and finds unrelated code, or trusts the 'first side-effecting step' framing when dnf install already ran.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the observability measurement cadence and what bounds the `du -sx` walk (e.g. timeout / nice+ionice / interval) so 'bounded' is a decision, not an adjective.
evidence: No stated cadence for the observability publish cycle, nor a definition of what makes the du 'bounded' (timeout? nice/ionice? cycle interval).
findings.finding: observability.sh runs a full-tree `du -sx` over /var/lib/docker (and over overlay2) each measurement cycle; the plan calls it 'bounded' but never states the measurement cadence or what bounds the du cost against a live daemon's I/O.
findings.location: Design → 'Detecting the bytes docker system df cannot see'; AC observability bullet
scenarios: On a host under active build/deploy load a repeated whole-tree du contends with Docker's own overlay2 I/O each cycle.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the retirement policy for daemon.json backups (fixed single `.bak`, or timestamped-with-pruning) so backups do not accumulate on the protected host.
evidence: Plan: 'daemon.json is BACKED UP and the merged file VALIDATED'
Plan: 'a failed validation restores the backup and changes nothing' — backup is created every re-run but the plan never states whether/when old backups are removed
T9 requires a RETIRE/cleanup path so shared state does not leak/accumulate; this is on the very host whose storage the plan is protecting
findings.finding: The daemon.json backup created on each compose-up.sh re-run has no stated retirement/cleanup path, so backups accumulate under the host filesystem across repeated runs.
findings.location: Design — 'Install point, and how a LIVE daemon picks it up' (`daemon.json` is BACKED UP)
scenarios: Repeated compose-up.sh re-runs on a long-lived host leave a growing set of daemon.json backup files that themselves consume disk on the host being protected
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that the backup uses a single stable path (e.g. `daemon.json.rebar.bak`) overwritten each run, or a timestamped backup with a documented retention count, and name the exact path the failed-validation restore reads from.
